beats.headline: Carl gets her inside
beats.text: The next episode is starting and the collapse is on top of us, and I am not, at my age, built for sprinting, or for walking. Carl, the young man with the cat, gets behind my wheelchair and pushes me into the storm shelter, and I let him, because I am old and not stupid. Then I ask him to put Divorce Court on the television. My Barry used to watch it.

beats.headline: The tunnel of love
beats.text: I'm on the last car of a train that rolls on wheelchair wheels, and the young man with the cat is walking beside me. I remember his name today. Carl. This reminds me of the tunnel of love. My Barry and I used to go to the carnival, and back then it was a boat, and I'd let him touch them, but only on the outside of my sweater. Barry wasn't pretty. If Carl were in that tunnel with me, I'd let him do more. He says thank you. I cackle.

beats.headline: Stuck to the ceiling
beats.text: One minute I'm on the last car, the next I'm on the roof of the hallway with my own wheelchair on top of me and my health deep in the red, and I start to cry. Carl picks me up like a sack and runs upside down, and then we fall. He gets me inside. Brandon helps me drink the potion. You saved me, I tell Carl. Thank you. Jack was always an ass. Poor Yolanda was such a good kid. Randall was dumb as a pigeon, but he deserved better. At least it was quick.

beats.headline: Barry, where are we?
beats.text: There's a nice young man kneeling by my bucket, and I ask him: Barry, where are we? He says we're in the dungeon, and I'm going down to the next floor. The dungeon? Like a sex thing? He says goodbye. I touch his cheek. We should have had children, Barry. I wish I hadn't talked you into working so hard. I think I've had too much to drink, or I'm having another one of those acid flashbacks. This cat keeps talking to me.

beats.headline: Tenth on the board
beats.text: Tenth on the draft leaderboard, spelled Elle McGib: Frost Maiden, Blizzardmancer, level thirteen, bounty one hundred thousand. She began the third floor at level one. Carl knows her as a wheelchair-bound resident of Meadow Lark and cannot work out how she got there; he has not talked to Brandon in several days.

beats.headline: On the board, two hours in
beats.text: Crawler Elle McGibbons, formerly of Meadow Lark, is seen on the recap for one second: a blue-skinned, white-haired elf thing that floats instead of walking, skewering a troll-like monster in a subway car with icicles shot from her palms. Race: Frost Maiden. Class: Blizzardmancer. Level: seventeen; the list the crawlers were shown before had her at fourteen. Leaderboard rank: ten. Bounty: one hundred thousand gold. Carl realises he has already seen her in passing on earlier recaps without knowing it was her.

beats.headline: Frost Maiden, for now
beats.text: I'm a Frost Maiden. For now. Blue, small, and I float, and yes, those are still the anti-slip socks. I had a long list of options that would've put all my marbles back in the bag, but Brandon made me pick this one, for the manager benefit Carl told him about. Mistress Tiatha actually cried. I got my club tattoo for an icicle up the keister of an orc bartender. There's twenty of us left, and Imani still acts like the babysitter. And Carl is buying this round.

beats.headline: You come for Donut, you come for us
beats.text: A woman in the crowd is about to blast Carl and the cat, so she gets a two-foot icicle through the eye socket from behind. There's a skull after my name now. Don't care. I call dibs on her gear and tell Donut to loot hers before we get thrown out. Then I tell the room: anybody comes for Donut or Carl comes for all of us, and I will freeze the blood in their veins. A dwarf gives me the eyeball. He backs up. Donut, don't you cry. This was inevitable, and once word gets out, nobody will mess with you again.

beats.headline: Stuck at 275
beats.text: We clear stop 275 on the Camel Line and kill one of those Krakaren bitches. Easier than Imani thought. Then the train to 277 never comes. Imani blames that Quan Ch fellow for blowing up trains. It's twenty or thirty miles to the next stop and another thirty after that, so instead we take the druggie portal back to 272 and hike down to 271. If the Cobalt line is out too, there's a named train there called the Eviscerator. We're out of commission for a day, at least. I tell Carl. He tells me to stay away from the third rail. Oh, you know it.

beats.headline: A way out of the robot rooms
beats.text: Hey, hotshot. Your instincts were right. There's a secret way out of the robot rooms: a long tunnel sloping downward. It doesn't open until the robots wake up, and they don't wake until the monsters start their withdrawal. Lucky us, we don't have to fight the metal bastards. I still can't believe you blew two of them up. We're following the tunnel now. Sounds like there's another train track down there. It's far. More when we know.

beats.headline: Now's our chance
beats.text: It is not a train. It is a roller coaster with no cars. The robots fill rolling cages with ghouls and push them down, the bottom catches on the track, and off they go, like the thing at the hospital that takes your trays away but a hell of a lot faster. Carl says if it were him he would take it, and that it is a huge gamble. By the time the good roller coasters came along I was too old for them, and my Barry puked cotton candy after the tilt-a-whirl. Now's our chance.

beats.headline: No cobra lady in the crowd
beats.text: Carl asked me to go through every single person here and I did. No four-armed cobra lady. There's a man who turned himself into a mushroom, which, why. The fairy with the two mage daughters says the woman isn't answering anyone; if she came in with us, she took off. Imani is mother-henning everybody, and they're all terrified of her. Then Carl throws a train full of explosives our way and knocks everybody off their feet. He's lucky I can fly. I think the mushroom guy soiled himself.

beats.headline: Asking the manager about mimics
beats.text: Carl wants to know if there's a secret way to kill a mimic, so I ask him: are you about to do something really stupid, or have you done it already? Both, he says. Our manager says you don't fight the giant ones. Slice a piece off and it grows legs and runs home. Get more than half the mass off at once and it can't heal or change shape, but the cut-off pieces come for you, and they only die when the mimic does. I also talked a group out of the province boss at 48. You can hear it screaming from here.

beats.headline: Icicles off a god
beats.text: I've got a scroll that lets me fly higher and faster than an old lady has any right to, and I spend it. Icicles off Grull's head, and then I shoot past him like a bullet. He swipes at me and nearly has me. Then he opens his mouth and a blast of heat comes out that melts everything in its path, and it misses me by inches. I land on a derailed train by the gate, next to Katia wearing Carl's face, and take off again.

beats.headline: Twenty of us, and a sailboat
beats.text: There are twenty of us on this boat and not one of these old farts has ever sailed. I told them not to put me in Meadow Lark. The system gives us a sailing tutorial that won't tell you where the boom vang is. We'd have an NPC to help if I hadn't iced him, but he was being suspicious. Then Imani crashes the boat and I have to freeze the water so nobody drowns. My deity box gave me a spellbook. Graupel. Big ice storm, fifty mana, long cooldown. Most powerful thing I've got, and I'm kinda scared to try it.

beats.headline: An oil rig that throws fireballs
beats.text: We're the only ones in the water quadrant. We've got ourselves a galley now, fish-people doing the rowing, and we're probing our castle: an oil rig run by orcs that shoots fireballs at anybody who gets close. We've seen the land crawlers but haven't talked to them. Their castle's an oil refinery. The whole bubble is some stupid story about how we earthlings ruined our own planet. The air castle's a storm cloud that rains acid, I think. You get saddled with a bunch of layabouts, Carl?

beats.headline: Somebody has to send it
beats.text: Imani won't send this one, so I will, word for word, from Chris: Carl, Donut. Please. Kill me. It's okay. I give you permission. Carl tells him where he can go, and I tell Chris the same thing. But if they can't find a fix, they don't have a choice. If it was me stuck in there, I'd want someone to pull the plug. I pass along the rest when it comes through: Maggie doesn't worship Grull, she worships a god called Algos. Then Chris gets cut off mid-sentence, messaging suspended for thirty minutes.

beats.headline: A god walked through our world
beats.text: We finally pop our bubble, and a god taller than the whole place walks straight through it. On fire. Flattens a Lyrx elf village, knocks over two of their oil derricks and lights them. Half the world is in flames. Imani and I are stuck in the Desperado; nearly everybody else had to run for the stairwell, and we're lucky nobody caught fire. He's looking for something. He keeps shouting "Orthrus." Something tells me this is Carl's doing, and I say so. He says maybe. Well, you better fix it.

beats.headline: This floor was a drag
beats.text: Imani and I open the portal on our world and get the changelings through to the next floor, Twister and all, then rush back to the club, dead on our feet. Katia gives me a long hug and tells us to be careful. We always are. I wink at Carl, pat the cat on the head, and hand over the three pieces of the gate. I am looking forward to mixing it up with these three again. This floor was a real drag, doing it all myself.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess
beats.text: There I am on the recap, for everyone: Blizzardmancer to Tundra Princess. Some sort of earth class, combined with the ice. And I get to pick yet another class on the ninth floor. Seventh on the top ten, Frost Maiden, level forty-seven. Carl and I have managed one quick check-in this floor and he didn't ask how I'd changed, so this is how the young man finds out.

beats.headline: Tundra Princess, level fifty-one
beats.text: Tundra Princess now, level fifty-one, and you'd never know it to look at me. Same anti-slip socks from Meadow Lark. Wedding ring on a chain, because my fingers shrank. I've got a glass of something yellow, and Louis is watching it like a dog watches jerky. Katia turned this whole circus around to come save your ass, young man, and then the flying house got jumped by pterodactyls, so now we're stuck in the jungle. How was the convention?

beats.headline: Level 173 and loving it
beats.text: That thing was huge. Level 173, and it poked holes all over the Twister's garden. Most fun I've had since we got to this ridiculous floor. The little dinosaur cat is sulking that hers was only 138. Carl's pointing us at the next one fifteen miles west, right up against the edge of the map, and Katia says we're already on it. Louis says he doesn't know if he can stomach it again.

beats.headline: Right above the church
beats.text: I was right above it when the church blew. Green smoke, like the mushroom spores but thicker. Gave me a buff against fire and poison. Five or six dryads went up pinwheeling blood, it all swirled into a giant flower, and the bud opened with that eyebrowless hunter inside. The gore poured into his mouth and he swelled like a can of potted meat on a cookfire. Out came an antlered squirrel no bigger than me. Diwata, sponsored by Circe Took. It flew off like a rocket. Mordecai wants the pollen. He can wade in himself.

beats.headline: What the hairless hunter told her
beats.text: I got the story out of that hunter with no eyebrows. Vrah messaged his brother, told him he'd be safe if he went into that temple, and tricked him into being the birthing vessel for Diwata. They murdered one of their own just to cure Vrah of a venereal disease, and the brother is pissed about it. Now the bug lady is birthing actual flesh-and-blood babies and sending them out into the world. What happens when the floor collapses? Do they just go away? They're her kids!

beats.headline: Cat-nac the Magnificent
beats.text: The queen's cat drops onto Carl's shoulder in a gold turban with a feather four feet high, and I lose it. Louis says goose. It's not a goose, it's one of those mushroom penises. It's Horton! Hey, Horton, you have merch! How do you even walk in that thing, cat? Should we call you Cat-nac the Magnificent? He promises to bathe in our offal. I tell Donut her ex-boyfriend has anger issues. She says she's always been attracted to the bad boys. You and me both, sister.

beats.headline: A bigfoot in Bermuda shorts
beats.text: First things first, Carl: skipping a level without warning us was messed up. Not all of us are as trained up as you. He swears it was all Pony. Then the boxes, and holy shitballs, I got an ice staff I won't stop talking about. And just now a goddamned bigfoot crossed the road in front of me wearing Bermuda shorts. He almost got splattered. So here's my idea, young man. We build the roadblocks away from the saferooms, so the pileups don't happen near the stairwells.

beats.headline: A snooze fest out west
beats.text: Carl asks in chat whether we're going into the Desperado Club. Imani tells him we still haven't found one. And it's a total snooze fest over here: all churches and boring monsters. I've got my squatchy and my gumberoo and my batsquatch, and everything else sucks. We don't even have any quests. So we're moving down to the outskirts of Portland to see if there's anything interesting there. Carl tells me to be careful.

beats.headline: Don't let her die, cowboy
beats.text: I tell Carl I hope he knows what he's doing, cowboy. If anything happens to her, Tony the Tiger goes, and there goes the tea he makes us every morning, which I'm fairly sure is the only thing holding Imani together. Imani and I are going to pick different places in phase two so they can't make us fight each other. My squatch squad will kick anybody's ass. I'd have bet good money on Louis cracking first. Poor kid. Louis says he's standing right here.

beats.headline: Not really them
beats.text: Belgium. I don't know anybody in Belgium, thank God. Imani's in Detroit and I'm not with her; my squad and I landed on our own, and everybody else is scattered to the four winds. So I tell the lot of them what needs telling. Keep your wits about you. These are just memory ghosts. If they're going to make us fight loved ones, remember it isn't really them. Don't let them mess with your heads.

beats.headline: She has a martyr complex
beats.text: Listen to me, young man. You have to figure this out. That girl has a martyr complex, and she's not going to want to fight anybody. She's a good kid. The best person I ever met, and we need her. Don't let her give up. Don't let her sacrifice herself. Me? I don't know who I'm facing yet.

beats.headline: At the church with the rest
beats.text: The church, and it is full. Imani is there, and then Katia's people, and then Li Na's, and then mine. My own squad. Every one of us got here on a Doggy Door upgrade that Lucia handed round before she took the stairs down. I do not know what that girl is. She gave us a way through, and I am standing in a church with my friends because of it, so I will say thank you and keep the rest of my opinions where they belong.

beats.headline: Graupel at level sixteen
beats.text: Graupel has a one week cooldown and I only ever cast it once before, on the fifth floor. It's a war spell, outdoors only. Somebody had to, so I float up and cast it at the mob coming for Donut. The spell says it's casting stronger than usual. It's only a level five spell and it goes off at level sixteen, and then the sky comes down in fist-sized hail. When the steam clears there's a field of dead demons as far as you can see, and I've gone up six levels at once. Seventy-two. A bunch of achievements. What the hell?

beats.headline: Tundra Princess to Hailstorm Queen
beats.text: Class selection again, in the warehouse, with only a few of us this time. I pick wind, and Tundra Princess becomes Hailstorm Queen. Donut is thrilled I'm a queen. This is probably as far as it goes: I can add the final element if I ever make it to the twelfth floor, but I'm betting this whole shitshow self-destructs before we get anywhere close.

beats.headline: I found out
beats.text: Back in our territory, young man. I'm pretty sure I've found every artillery battery on both sides, though I can't swear to a hundred per cent. And we've got a new problem. They have another nasty surprise waiting for us on the naga side. Remember when you asked me to find out why those robot fellows wanted pet levelling sped up? Well. I found out.

beats.headline: The first anti-air gun
beats.text: Man, I wish I could cast my Graupel spell. Can't, so it's Carl's missile launcher, and I hope it works as advertised. Carl says for god's sake keep moving. Louis drops, and I fire. First anti-air gun: hit, but it had a protection spell on it. It went over, though, and with luck it won't be firing for a while. Moving to the second one.

beats.headline: Second battery down
beats.text: The second anti-air battery is down! Louis, hurry your ass up. The first one's almost back up already, and I'm running, because they've a pair of mages on my scent. Imani says get the hell out of there. Then I tell Louis his path to the enemy castle is free of anti-air guns, as far as I can see.

beats.headline: The goat got there first
beats.text: Holy hell, Carl, get in position. Everything's fouled up. Most of their army is already dead, corpses rotting in the barracks; Edgar found them on his scan. And the moment we moved in, that goat friend of yours appeared out of nowhere and went apeshit. He's level 99 now. He didn't attack us, but he called me every name there is, and when Imani told him to calm down he called her a festering gutter maggot trollop. So the sluggalos went after him. Half are sliming across naga territory, whooping. The other half took one of the carts. Driving it? Not very well.

beats.headline: He pulled back at the last moment
beats.text: Sorry, guys. That war mage prick snatched the gate right out of my hands. I haven't been walloped like that since my bachelorette party. Samantha laughed. Carl did not. But listen, Carl, they could've killed me. The strong one, the elf-looking guy, pulled back at the last moment. It was almost like he was trying not to kill me. Now collect the bodies. They said the heads explode. Then let me cast Subterfuge again, and are you ready to finally get your hands dirty?

beats.headline: A goddamn hero
beats.text: For chrissakes. We were only out of it for about an hour. In that Witness spell, all piled up, we were paralysed and felt everything; the moment Donut cast Battle Formation, it was lights out. Now she's apologising to everyone. My throat feels like I gargled sandpaper and I smell like that god's schlong, and that's it. We lost people from the towers when we woke. Some got burned by fleshers. Several lost limbs. She pulled through for all of us anyway, in a way nobody else could. Not even Carl. She's a goddamn hero.

beats.headline: The superfan
beats.text: A fan meet-and-greet, like the Butcher's Masquerade, name tag and everything, in a huge room. One guy came. A soother. Bought his own yacht to get through the quarantine and meet me, and he is standing there blushing in a shirt with a cartoon of me with no clothes on. Now he wants me to sign a giant pillow with me on it, and they have not even got my anatomy right. My nipples are not blue. If this place did not have safe room rules, I would have iced him already.

beats.headline: Under the table
beats.text: Imani and I drew a military vehicle that handles like a three-legged pig walking backward through a snowstorm, and Florin informs me it is one of the finest troop carriers in the world. Lovely. Under our table, wrapped round the leg, is my one fan, Linus, in his fanny pack and his shirt of me with no clothes on, because that is where little perverts sit when they ask stupid questions. Five hundred tourists were meant to win extra access to their favourite racer after each heat. He is the only one who came, so he wins by default.

beats.headline: She crushes one of Akuma's
beats.text: Donut mutes him. That part was planned. The ice bolt to the crotch was mine, and so is the rest. That little magical fart and his friends tried to kill me and stole my Gate before I was done with it. When I was a kid we hit thieves with sticks and threw their shoes in the sound. Now I can freeze a man's balls and break them like dollar store ornaments. That was just the left one. He answers everything Carl asks, or the right one goes too.

beats.headline: Five bucks on the ex-husband
beats.text: Cascadia's on the speaker, drunk, telling us somebody called Cumberland is dead. Five bucks says it's her ex-husband. It is. You haven't seen bitter until you've seen a woman work out after fifty years of marriage that her husband was a cheating idiot. We had plenty at Meadow Lark. Francine Herrada tried to throat-stab the new wife with a knitting needle, and I called her Killer after, and she didn't care for it. Mind you, she said spice in food was a sin. That poor husband.

beats.headline: Barry's song, and the impostor
beats.text: I'm not much for speeches, so I talk about Barry. Bartholomew Eli McGibbons, forty-three years my husband, thirty-five years gone. Louis hits play and it's Creedence, his favourite. He wouldn't have survived five minutes in this place. Then I float over to Linus. My fan club, the Snow Cones, knew an impostor the moment he stepped into the dungeon, and the real Linus's friends posted his essay where we could all read it. You keep coming in here to kill us, sweetheart. This is our house now.

beats.headline: Die with hope in our hearts
beats.text: Don't you worry about those tracksuit idiots, Donut. They had a way out, they lied to us, and they'd have killed me, Imani and Chris at that exit. Ivan bragged about pulling down a whole metal bridge for scrap and wrecking a train. Carl asks if it's true. Does it matter? Look at us, risking our necks again to save a few people. It matters whether a crazy Carl plan works, sure, we die if it doesn't. But we'll die with hope in our hearts alongside our friends.

beats.headline: A sign for the viewers
beats.text: Betrayal float. Mannequins in chairs in front of televisions, black and red smoke off the top, and signs. Imani's says you are watching real people die. Mine is at the very end: To all the viewers of Dungeon Crawler World: Earth: Fuck you. The back is a very detailed middle finger. The AI calls ours its favourite. Whew. We had an interpretive dance group at Meadow Lark once, and that made more sense than its story.

beats.headline: Folded in the APV
beats.text: I'm alive. Barely. Me and Bodi are stuck in what's left of the truck after the god blew up, and somebody had better dig us out. It's wrecked pretty good. I haven't been folded like this since Brandon showed us how to use Tinder. Imani is shouting my name on the chat. I'm here, Imani.

relations.note: She opened the gate that brought him
